result.topic_en: From a point inside a triangle, perpendiculars are dropped to the three sides; the page relates the perpendiculars, the segments they cut off on the sides, and the three quadrilaterals they enclose, then specialises to the case of three equal quadrilaterals.
result.transcription:
Math 26
(10) [-47-] [-12-]
[Figure: triangle with a point inside and perpendiculars $p, p', p''$ to the sides; segments $q, q', q''$ marked on the sides]
Es seien
$a, a', a''$ die Seiten eines Dreiecks
$p, p', p''$ die von einem beliebigen Punkt darauf gefällten Perpendikel
$q, q', q''$ die von den Perpendikeln auf den Seiten abgeschnittenen Stücke, nach einerlei Zählung genommen
$V, V', V''$ die zwischen je zwei Perpendikeln u. zwei Seiten enthaltenen Vierecke

so ist
(I) $p^2+q^2 = p''^2+(a''-q'')^2$
$p'^2+q'^2 = p^2+(a-q)^2$
$p''^2+q''^2 = p'^2+(a'-q')^2$

(II) $pq+p''(a''-q'') = 2V'$
$p'q'+p(a-q) = 2V''$
$p''q''+p'(a'-q') = 2V$

Je nachdem man die Gleichungen (I) u. 2(II) respective addirt oder von einander abzieht, erhält man
$(p+q)^2-(p''+q''-a'')^2 = 4V'$ \quad $(p''-q''+a'')^2-(p-q)^2 = 4V'$
$(p'+q')^2-(p+q-a)^2 = 4V''$ \quad $(p-q+a)^2-(p'-q')^2 = 4V''$
$(p''+q'')^2-(p'+q'-a')^2 = 4V$ \quad $(p'-q'+a')^2-(p''-q'')^2 = 4V$

Wenn $V=V'=V''$ u. man setzt
$p+q=2x\sqrt{V}$; $p'+q'=2x'\sqrt{V}$; $p''+q''=2x''\sqrt{V}$
$a=2c\sqrt{V}$; $a'=2c'\sqrt{V}$; $a''=2c''\sqrt{V}$
so wird
$x^2-(x''-c'')^2=1$
$x'^2-(x-c)^2=1$
$x''^2-(x'-c')^2=1$
\hline
$2cx+2c'x'+2c''x''=3+c^2+c'^2+c''^2$

methods.what: Pythagorean relations: the distance from the interior point to a vertex is computed in two ways from the adjacent perpendiculars and side segments
Area of each quadrilateral formed by two perpendiculars and two sides, expressed as a sum of two right triangles
Adding or subtracting (I) and 2(II) gives difference-of-squares expressions for 4 times the quadrilateral areas
Normalisation by $\sqrt{V}$ in the case of equal quadrilaterals, giving hyperbola-type relations
Summing the three normalised relations gives a linear relation between the $x$'s and the $c$'s
